items.title: Serre criterion for affineness
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs global functions from the H1 vanishing hypothesis and obtains affine principal neighbourhoods. It then combines a finite principal-open cover with a unit-ideal argument to prove affineness; the covering construction is part of the problem rather than an assumed affineness criterion.

items.title: Chow lemma for separated finite-type morphisms over a Noetherian base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a quasi-projective proper modification of a separated finite-type scheme over a Noetherian base using closures of diagonal graph maps. Scheme-theoretic density permits gluing the local projections and proves exact inverse-image identities; these verify properness, surjectivity and a dense-open isomorphism. This is a substantive geometric construction beyond routine qualifying algebra.

items.title: Stein factorization with geometrically connected fibres
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The relative spectrum of the direct image gives a finite factorization, but the proof must also establish geometrically connected fibres. The included normalization and proper-fibre arguments carry the nontrivial part of this claim.

items.title: Lazard characterization of flat modules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof turns finite relations in a flat module into factorizations through finite free modules. These factorizations construct a directed system whose colimit is the original module, proving the nontrivial direction of Lazard characterization.

items.title: Miracle flatness
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The dimension equality permits the choice of an element that is a regular parameter of the source and a nonzerodivisor of the Cohen-Macaulay target. Quotienting lowers both dimensions, allowing induction, and the local flatness criterion then lifts flatness from the quotient.

items.title: Openness of fibrewise exactness for finite free complexes over flat finite-type algebras over a Noetherian base with Cohen-Macaulay fibres of fixed dimension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The author spreads exactness from one localized fibre through determinantal rank bounds and converts the remaining grade conditions into regular-sequence conditions in the fibres. Cohen-Macaulay dimensional control makes these conditions open, giving a substantive family-wise exactness criterion beyond ordinary module exactness tests.

items.title: Decomposition and classification of injective modules over a Noetherian ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a direct-sum decomposition by transfinite recursion, splitting off injective hulls detected by associated primes. The limit-ordinal stages must remain injective and preserve the direct-sum structure; this is a structural classification task beyond routine finite module arguments.

items.title: Explicit Cech construction of the right adjoint for derived torsion complexes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs the right adjoint on the unbounded derived category by an extended Cech total complex. It proves torsion of its cohomology using a filtered colimit of Koszul complexes and null homotopies, then proves the counit is invertible on the torsion subcategory. These are actual derived-category construction obligations rather than substitution into a local-cohomology formula.

items.title: Greenlees-May identities relating derived completion and local cohomology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: Both identities are proved by constructing and filtering the two different mapping cones. The graded pieces are derived Hom from localizations or localized derived tensor products, and distinct vanishing mechanisms annihilate them. The task requires compatible control of derived completion and torsion on arbitrary complexes.

items.title: The image of the unit under an A-linear coherent derived equivalence is invertible
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The argument first forces the image of every residue field to be concentrated in one degree by ruling out negative self-extensions. It then detects all remaining cohomology of the image of A using finite-length test modules, Nakayama, and endomorphism rings. Recovering local shifts of rank-one free modules from categorical data is a substantive reconstruction argument.

items.title: Amplitude, support dimension and depth of duals of finite local modules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof establishes three simultaneous bounds for dualizing Ext modules by induction on support dimension. The positive-depth case uses a regular element, boundary nonvanishing and support-dimension inequalities; the depth-zero case removes the finite-length torsion and reconstructs the result through a long exact sequence. The support and exact nonvanishing obligations exceed ordinary depth calculations.

items.title: Support and Serre S2 property of the canonical module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The support is identified using normalized localizations, the dimension function and catenarity. The S2 bound is proved by dimension induction, with separate regular-element and depth-zero torsion-removal arguments. The canonical module must satisfy two depth conditions even when the original local ring has depth zero.

items.title: Gorenstein ascent and descent for flat local ring homomorphisms
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof compares residue-field Ext over the base and total rings through flat base change and a restriction right adjoint. In the descent direction it extracts the exact single-degree fibre dualizing complex after proving the base Gorenstein by faithful flatness. This controls injective dimension and the closed fibre simultaneously.

items.title: Gorenstein formal fibres of a local ring with a dualizing complex
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The argument reduces every formal fibre to the generic fibre of a domain quotient. It then tracks the dualizing complex through completion and fraction-field localization and proves the formal-fibre dualizing object is a shift of the unit. The compatibility of completion and the generic dualizing shift is a substantive structural obligation.

items.title: Identification of upper shriek with derived Hom for finite ring maps
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof reduces a general finite algebra to a monogenic quotient by a monic polynomial using transitivity. It constructs the dual basis action explicitly and shows the coefficient functional generates the algebra dual as a rank-one module. The resulting comparison identifies independently constructed derived functors, not merely their underlying complexes.

items.title: Expression of algebraic upper shriek by dualizing biduality
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The polynomial-algebra case is proved through bounded injective models and a truncation argument valid for potentially unbounded coherent complexes. The surjection case uses a derived tensor-Hom adjunction chain and Yoneda; composition then assembles arbitrary finite-type maps. Establishing this functorial identification demands more than the existence of dualizing complexes.

items.title: Fibre-dimension bounds and relative Tor amplitude of a flat relative dualizing complex
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: Besides cohomological bounds, the proof must establish uniform Tor amplitude against arbitrary modules over the base. It uses arbitrary Noetherian base change followed by square-zero extensions to detect derived tensor with finite modules, then filtered colimits. This passage from geometric fibre bounds to all-module Tor bounds is nonroutine.

items.title: Existence and arbitrary base change of relative dualizing complexes for flat finitely presented algebras
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof first descends the algebra to a finite-type integer model. For arbitrary non-Noetherian base changes it builds a relatively flat Hom model, proves universal injectivity and flatness of its successive cokernels by residue-field testing, and identifies degree-zero cohomology compatibly with the rigidifying generator. These are the core construction and base-change obligations.

items.title: Localization on the base of the right adjoint for proper pushforward
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof detects a hypothetical support violation with a perfect complex, lifts that detection across the open immersion, and annihilates its adjoint map by a perfect complex on the base. The projection formula then gives a contradiction while preserving the nonzero restricted map. The actual support control of the adjoint is a nonroutine argument.

items.title: Tor-independent base change for the right adjoint of proper pushforward
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The argument tests the canonical base-change map against a perfect generator and compares two global derived Hom complexes. It separately controls perfect and pseudo-coherent pushforward hypotheses, then proves the constructed identification is exactly the specified natural transformation through a large adjunction diagram. Identifying the map, rather than only isomorphic objects, is a core obligation.
